WHAT WAS MEASURED (all LOSE vs the 58ms cluster; the 768 dominant block is GENUINELY CLUSTER-BOUND):
- t1 route k=768 reduced Bk -> cuSOLVER syevd: shape 10 +4.9% (63ms > 58ms cluster; matches the code note cluster 63.7 vs cuSOLVER 67.3).
- t2/t4 sign-DC split the FORMED 768 Bk into 2x~402 megakernel (+accuracy stack half_reorth/side_membership/count_select in t4): +102%, 60/60 cuSOLVER fallback. Profile: the 402-block megakernel is only 7ms/FAST, but the split mass-falls-back (25ms symv+17ms gemvx+laed3 = cuSOLVER) + 27ms CQR2/lift overhead.
- t3 rank probe k=608: 60/60 fallback -- confirms nearrank has EXACT rank 768 (sig spectrum logspace(-1,0,768)=[0.1,1.0]); k<768 misses eigenpairs, complement Rayleigh can't represent them.
- t5/t6 nested MAGNITUDE-peel (deflate: top-448 Q1 -> B1 megakernel; project-off-Q1 next-320 Q2 -> B2 megakernel; free 256 tail), power 1 then 2: 60/60 fallback. rescued=0 (NS reorth doesn't fix -> it's an EIGEN-residual/missing-subspace miss, not orthogonality).

ROOT CAUSE (robust, profiled across t2/t4/t5/t6): the 768 SIGNIFICANT eigenvalues are DENSELY PACKED in [0.1,1.0] (spacing ~0.0012, no gap). ANY 2-way split into <=448 chunks -- sign-based OR magnitude-deflation -- cuts through a dense eigenvalue cluster; the boundary eigenvectors (~rank 448) are near-degenerate across chunks, so each reduced block gets a partial copy -> the assembled V misses those eigenpairs -> gate fails -> full-batch cuSOLVER. Splitting requires a spectral gap that this spectrum does not have. The single 768-block (parent) captures all 768 in ONE subspace with no internal boundary -- why it works and every split fails. The cluster kernel is the only primitive faster than cuSOLVER for the whole 768-block.
